plant.verbatim: small, unrecognizable except the fire; colouring quite good

seat.BEST_WHY: The wall-base band along the top of the room (y≈420–450, x≈185–505 and x≈565–750) is the best-made thing in the deck: a dark timber rail with lighter driven posts at irregular spacing, the rope/lashing texture sitting *on* the stone rather than replacing it, and it darkens with distance the same way the floor does — so it reads as one surface under one light. The wall tops in the upper-left block (x≈120–500, y≈70–400) carry cracks that fork and terminate rather than continue as a single stroke, and the corridor mouth at (505–565, 440) has a clean corner where the wall face meets the wall top. The figure's light falls off smoothly with no banding anywhere in the gradient. Nothing in this frame is a placed object, so nothing has been pasted on.
seat.WORST_WHY: It is a stamped tileset with no lighting and no wear model. The grey wall along the bottom (y≈205–290) repeats the same brick arrangement every 32 px with identical mortar — you can count the seams. The dirt floor is one speckle texture repeated with no variation; the "wear" spots on the left wall at (≈20,60) and (≈10,210) are the same lighter blob stamped twice. The green pool (x≈250–355, y≈0–190) meets the floor along a hard straight line with no bank, lip or wet edge — a water tile butted against a dirt tile. The hearth at (≈30,130) is drawn in side elevation with the fire visible through its front, while the walls around it are top-down; the two crates at (≈80,15) and (≈80,60) are the same sprite at full saturation with a black outline that nothing else in the frame has. It looks like the free one.

flip_list_withheld: There is a straight hard edge in the lighting running from about (505,445) diagonally to (745,800) with nothing casting it; the rest of the light is soft radial, so this reads as an unsmoothed shadow polygon. Either give it a caster the player can see or soften it to match the falloff.

The crate at (≈250,500) is a saturated orange-red box with a flat pale rectangle for a top; it is the only thing in the frame that colour. Bring it into the scene's palette and give the top a plank or hide texture.
The bound timber at (≈440,615) and the standing stone at (≈280,590) have no ground contact — the stone in particular floats over the crack it should be sitting on. Add a contact shadow to both.

The wall tops in the upper-left block go to near-black much faster than in frame 1 (compare the crack lines that are visible at (300,200) in 1 and gone in 4); the ambient floor has been dropped too far and the walls have lost their structure.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08
panel.seat_plant_stop: 3 seats missed a live plant in one round (seats 2, 4, 5). That is not one seat having a bad day.

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
